hook: An immune receptor's TIR domain makes a molecule and keeps it as glue to assemble its signaling complex.
hook_turn: and keeps it as glue to assemble its signaling complex.
summary: The TLR4 TIR domain turns out to be an enzyme that breaks down NAD+ once, when allosterically activated. The product, ADP-ribose, stays trapped and helps bind the adaptor TIRAP into a complex that starts signaling. This changes the view of animal TIR domains as passive scaffolds, though the work is biochemical and structural rather than in whole animals.
title: A trapped catalytic product acts as molecular glue for innate immune signalosome assembly.
